title: Making the Job Offer: Getting Your Offer Letter Right
author: Mawingu HR Solutions
shortDescription: The offer stage is where a great hiring process can quietly fall apart. How to make an offer that is clear, competitive and legally sound — and turns a yes into a signature.
body:
You have found the right person. Now comes a step that many small businesses rush or bungle: the offer. A vague verbal "we'd love to have you" followed by a scramble over terms can lose a good candidate or, worse, create a dispute before day one. A clear, well-made offer closes the gap between "yes" and a signed start.

Make the offer clearly

Once you have decided, move promptly — good candidates have other options. Make the offer warmly, then follow it immediately with a written offer letter so nothing rests on memory. Speed and clarity here signal that you are organised and serious.

What the offer letter should state

  • Job title and start date.
  • Gross salary and pay frequency, plus any allowances or benefits.
  • Place and hours of work, including whether the role is on-site, remote or hybrid.
  • Probation period and its length.
  • Any conditions — for example satisfactory references or required documents.
  • A clear acceptance step — how and by when to confirm.
Be explicit that the salary is gross and that statutory deductions apply. The "but I thought that was my take-home" conversation is entirely avoidable.

Avoid the common traps

Confusing gross and net pay is the classic one — state gross and note that PAYE, SHIF, NSSF and the Housing Levy are deducted. Do not make promises verbally that are not in the letter. And make sure the offer letter and the eventual contract agree with each other, so you are not signing two documents that say different things.

From offer to contract

The offer letter opens the door; the employment contract is the full agreement. Have the signed contract ready for the start date, consistent with the offer. Handling this stage crisply leaves the new hire's very first impression of you as an organised, trustworthy employer — exactly the note you want to start on.
